title: Towers with epimorphic transitions have no derived limit terms
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with small pro-étale site $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and let $\mathcal R$ be a sheaf of rings on this site.
Let $(M_n,t_n)_{n\geq0}$ be a tower of sheaves of $\mathcal R$-modules
[def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with epimorphic transition maps
$t_n\colon M_{n+1}\to M_n$. Put $P=\prod_{n\geq0}M_n$ and let $T\colon P\to P$
be the morphism whose $n$th coordinate is $t_n$ composed with the $(n+1)$st projection.
Use the convention $R\varprojlim_nM_n=\operatorname{Cone}(1-T)[-1]$ of
[det-pe-milnor-sequence], and $R^p\varprojlim_nM_n=H^p(R\varprojlim_nM_n)$.
Write $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal R)$ for the derived category of these module
sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Then $1-T\colon P\to P$ is an epimorphism,
$R^1\varprojlim_nM_n=0$, and the canonical map from the ordinary inverse limit [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]
$\varprojlim_nM_n[0]\to R\varprojlim_nM_n$ is an isomorphism in
$D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal R)$.

proof.text: Fix an affine weakly contractible object $W$. By [det-pe-sections-limits-colimits], evaluation $\Gamma(W,-)$ on $\mathcal R$-modules preserves all limits and colimits. In particular $P(W)=\prod_n M_n(W)$ and it preserves cokernels and the zero object. Since $t_n$ is an epimorphism, $\coker t_n=0$, hence $\coker(t_n(W))=(\coker t_n)(W)=0$. A module homomorphism has zero cokernel exactly when its image is its target (its cokernel is the quotient by its image). Thus every $t_n(W)$ is surjective. This uses the module-valued evaluation statement, without assuming that an arbitrary epimorphism of sheaves is surjective on arbitrary objects.

source.place: first two sentences: surjectivity of t_n(W) and product evaluation

proof.text: For an arbitrary $a=(a_n)\in\prod_n M_n(W)$, choose, using the surjectivity in step 1, a set-theoretic right inverse $s_n\colon M_n(W)\to M_{n+1}(W)$ of each $t_n(W)$. Define $m_0=0$ and $m_{n+1}=s_n(m_n-a_n)$ recursively. The induction is well-defined: if $m_n\in M_n(W)$, then $m_n-a_n\in M_n(W)$ and $m_{n+1}\in M_{n+1}(W)$. For every $n\geq0$ one has $t_n(W)(m_{n+1})=m_n-a_n$, so $((1-T)(W)(m))_n=m_n-t_n(W)(m_{n+1})=a_n$. Therefore $(1-T)(W)$ is surjective. The choices are made separately for each $W$; no compatible choices with respect to restrictions, and no splitting in the sheaf category, are asserted.

source.place: Given (a_n), put m_0=0 and choose recursively m_{n+1}; displayed coordinate calculation

proof.text: For every affine weakly contractible $W$, step 2 says that $P(W)\xrightarrow{(1-T)(W)}P(W)\to0$ is exact at the second term. Apply assertion 1 of [det-pe-sections-conservative] to the sequence $P\xrightarrow{1-T}P\to0$, whose composite is zero. It is exact at the second term as a sequence of module sheaves. Thus the image of $1-T$ is all of $P$, or equivalently its cokernel is zero, and $1-T$ is an epimorphism.

source.place: So 1-T is surjective on every such W; sections-conservative detects exactness

proof.text: Apply assertion 2 of [det-pe-milnor-sequence] to the given tower of modules concentrated in degree zero. It identifies $R^1\varprojlim_n M_n$ with $\coker(1-T)$, which vanishes by step 3, identifies $H^0(R\varprojlim_n M_n)$ with $\varprojlim_nM_n$, and gives zero cohomology in every degree outside $\{0,1\}$. In particular the derived limit has cohomology only in degree zero.

source.place: By det-pe-milnor-sequence, 2: cokernel and higher cohomology vanishing

proof.text: Identify the inverse limit with the kernel of 1-T by product and limit universal properties. The single-complex functor preserves products and limits, so the tuple of actual limit projections remains a kernel in cochain complexes. Its target endomorphism is epic: it is conjugate under the product comparison isomorphism to the single-complex image of the already epic sheaf endomorphism. Apply lem-weil-degreewise-epi-kernel-cocone-qis. Its two projection identities identify its comparison with the existing milnorLimitComparison, whose first component is the tuple of limit projections and whose second component is zero. Thus this particular canonical comparison is a quasi-isomorphism, and localization makes it an isomorphism.

source.place: last sentence: the kernel inclusion into the two-term complex is a quasi-isomorphism

proof_origin.place: The same five-step blueprint proof; the final kernel/cone comparison uses the proved generic degreewise-epimorphism kernel comparison, with its projection identities checked against the existing canonical map (V5).
